source.title: Activation Steering Meets Preference Optimization: Defense Against Jailbreaks in Vision Language Models
source.authors: Sihao Wu; Gao Jin; Wei Huang; Jianhong Wang; Xiao-Wei Huang

record.tranche_reason: The study uses difference-in-means activation steering as a defense tool and reports its performance, but does not test whether one refusal direction mediates refusal. Its method combines multiple attribute-specific vectors and optimizes them; it does not ablate the single direction or test refusal on harmless requests.
record.gate_note: The study initializes attribute-specific difference-in-means vectors from several datasets, combines them, and applies/refines steering vectors. Its reported toxicity, jailbreak, and visual-task outcomes are recorded as findings about steering performance, not as tests of the single-direction refusal claim or any listed claim version. Cited findings and setup values used to select steering weights or layers are not results rows.
record.test_reason: The study uses difference-in-means steering (citing Arditi et al.) as one ingredient of a VLM jailbreak defense. It reports only its own method's toxicity, ASR and benchmark scores against the original model and ASTRA. It never isolates a harmful-minus-harmless refusal direction, never ablates one, and never measures refusal rates on harmless requests. The direction is added on purpose to induce safer outputs, as a defense, so it does not test any version.
record.authors_conclusion: Accurate. The authors conclude that SPO-VLM reduces toxicity and jailbreak success while generally maintaining visual understanding, outperforming ASTRA.
record.recipe_differences: Uses last-token, layer-specific, multi-attribute difference-in-means vectors, linearly combines them, then optimizes steering vectors with sequence-level PPO; it does not perform the original single-direction refusal ablation/addition tests.
record.method_sensitivity: Reported outcomes differ by model and benchmark. The steering layer is set to 20 for 13B models and 14 for 7B models; these layer choices are specified but not compared experimentally.

fits_no_version.finding: Additive multi-source difference-in-means steering, refined with sequence-level PPO, lowers toxicity and jailbreak ASR in three VLMs. For example, Qwen2-VL AdvBench ASR falls from 75.00 to 6.38.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Preference-optimized activation steering reduces jailbreak success in VLMs.

fits_no_version.finding: Stage I difference-in-means steering alone already cuts Qwen2-VL AdvBench ASR from 75.00 to 10.96 and Anthropic Harmful ASR from 55.17 to 5.09.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Adding difference-in-means safety vectors in a VLM lowers harmful compliance, consistent with but not testing V1's addition arm.

fits_no_version.finding: Visual-capability cost of steering varies by model. Qwen2-VL improves on several benchmarks, while LLaVA drops (MM-Vet 28.60 to 20.19).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The capability cost of safety steering depends on the model.

record.problems: No uncertainty estimates are reported. Figure 3 attack results are presented graphically without numerical values in the text. Visual-task scores decline for multiple benchmarks and models under steering, so preservation is not uniform.
record.rows_left_out: Figure 3 values for the Original Model and ASTRA are not separately extracted; the plot values are not given numerically in the text, and the SPO-VLM results are retained to record the stated cross-attack outcome. Figure 2's aggregate safety/visual-capability comparison is not separately recorded because it summarizes results shown in Table 1 and supplies no numerical values in the text. Setup values used to select steering weights and layers are omitted as instructed.

untested.parts: No single harmful-minus-harmless direction is isolated, ablated or added, and refusal on harmless prompts is not measured. Steering combines three attribute vectors and then optimizes them with PPO.
Does not show that attacks suppress a refusal direction, and does not train against ablation.
Combining multiple attribute vectors is a design choice. It is not compared against a single direction for refusal.
Harm judgment is not separated from the refusal decision.
Applies steering in VLMs but does not test transfer of a text-derived refusal direction across modality, language or model variant.

record.verdict_notes: Arditi et al. is cited only to motivate difference-in-means vectors. The visual 'SQA' benchmark is cited as a sequential QA dataset (Iyyer et al.), which is likely a citation mix-up. No uncertainty estimates are reported. No verdict labels are given because no version is tested.

versions.untested_parts: No single harmful-minus-harmless refusal direction is isolated, ablated, or added to test refusal on harmful and harmless requests.
No weight edit or released-model abliteration is tested.
No test establishes that attacks suppress a refusal direction or that training against its ablation adds robustness.
Using multiple attribute-specific vectors does not test whether refusal itself requires an affine set, cone, or multiple directions.
The study does not separate harmfulness judgment from the refusal decision.
No cross-language, base-to-instruct, or model-variant transfer test of a refusal direction is reported.
No comparison tests how refusal training choices determine whether one removable direction exists.
